newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch raise petrol, diesel excise from July 1.
newsitem.headline: Dutch raise petrol, diesel excise from July 1.

text.p: Excise on gasoline and diesel in the Netherlands will increase from Tuesday, the Dutch finance ministry said on Monday.
The excise on gasoline will rise by 13 guilder cents (11.2 percent) to 1.29 guilders, that on diesel by six cents (8.6 percent) to 76 cents and that on LPG by 9.5 cents to 14.5 cents.
The increases are not a revenue-raising move as drivers will be compensated in the form of lower car tax.
Users of heavy goods vehicles, who already pay the lowest rate of vehicle tax allowed under European Union rules, will receive direct financial compensation.
Service stations within 20 km of the German border are also eligible for compensation for business lost to their cheaper German counterparts.

Consumers can expect to feel the impact of the excise increases immediately. Shell said last week it would increase its prices for all petrol grades by 13 cents from Tuesday, putting premium unleaded up to 2.17 guilders per litre.
